solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Henry locates rotten onion

indicators.note: something rotten has gone bad and fallen apart, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Henry tracks down an onion that has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot-like bulb; this is an old name for the shallot, a small mild member of the onion family.

clue.text: Neuritis affected Asiatic chap at first

indicators.note: affected here means altered or acted upon, so the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word chap

explanation.surface: An Asian man is suffering from inflamed nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes the C of 'chap', which joins ASIATIC before 'affected' shuffles the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: The condition is pain from the irritated sciatic nerve, a kind of nerve inflammation running down the leg.

clue.text: Nurse with facile way to attract sailors' attention

parts.note: to nurse a grudge is to harbour it, keep it in mind
facile means easy, undemanding, which is light as in light reading

explanation.surface: A nurse has an easy trick for getting the notice of seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurse' reads as the noun, but it is the verb meaning to keep a feeling alive.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon at a port entrance guides ships at night, signalling to mariners where safe water lies.

clue.text: Snare under waterfall for small bird

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed below the other piece, so after it

parts.note: lin, also spelt linn, is a Scottish word for a waterfall
a net is a snare for catching game

explanation.surface: A trap set beneath a cascade to catch a little songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: A common brown finch of Europe, a small songbird once kept as a cage bird.

clue.text: Turncoat backtracks, trapping second despot

indicators.note: trapping means holding another piece within it
backtracks tells us to read the word for a turncoat from right to left

parts.note: a rat is a deserter or traitor, one who changes sides

explanation.surface: A traitor retraces his steps and captures a tyrant's deputy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backtracks' turns RAT into TAR, and 'trapping' then puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian emperor ruled with absolute power, a classic example of an autocrat.

clue.text: Strong rod to clean rough encrustation on hull

parts.note: a bar is a strong rigid rod of metal or wood

indicators.note: rough suggests the letters are roughly handled and come out in disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone uses a stout pole to scrape off a crust on a ship's bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clean' reads as the job being done to the hull, but it is only fodder that 'rough' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: These crustaceans cling to ships' bottoms in crusty clusters, the classic growth that fouls a vessel below the waterline.

clue.text: Beat black flesh

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or beat someone
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Pound the dark meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat from a young sheep is a common kind of flesh eaten as food.

clue.text: Rescue disreputable rip arrested by bailiff once

indicators.note: arrested by means held inside the other piece

parts.note: a reeve was a medieval steward or bailiff

indicators.note: disreputable suggests disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rogue is seized by an old-time officer and then let off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks the bailiff as a historical office, the medieval steward of a manor.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay of punishment or a last-minute pardon saves someone, so it works as a noun for deliverance.

clue.text: Spread grease around a soft marine plant

indicators.note: around means placed outside the other pieces
spread means scattered about, so the letters of this word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
p, from piano, is the musical notation for soft

explanation.surface: Smear lubricant over a gentle sea-dwelling weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' makes SEAGRE from GREASE, and 'around' wraps it round A and P.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical seaside plant with grape-like clusters, either a coastal shrub or a gulfweed, grows by or in salt water.

clue.text: Wooden frame for carrying European booze

definitions.meaning: a stand on which a coffin is carried to the grave

explanation.surface: A wooden carrying frame with Continental drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffins rest on this movable stand at funerals; in German the same spelling names the beer.

clue.text: Is 17 as this

parts.note: the clue's own number, eleven, written in base two as 1 1, has the value of the answer at 17 across

explanation.surface: Reads like a cross-reference to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue number 11, read as base-two digits, equals the number at 17 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Written in base two, the digits one-one have the value of the small number given at 17.

clue.text: Knightly badge from corselet trimmed in the greater part

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: the mass of something is its bulk or majority

indicators.note: trimmed here means reshaped or rearranged, so the letters of the garment are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An emblem of knighthood cut from a bodice and set into the main portion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trimmed' looks like a deletion signal, but nothing is cut: every letter of the garment is reshaped.
explanation.definitionFit: The eight-pointed emblem of the Knights Hospitaller of St John is the insignia of that order.

clue.text: Set and positioned Greek letter back inside

indicators.note: inside means placed within the other piece

parts.note: to set something somewhere is to site it

indicators.note: back tells us to read the Greek letter from right to left

parts.note: tau is the Greek letter T

explanation.surface: Arranged and placed, with a Greek character turned round within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set and positioned' looks like a single definition; 'Set' is the container and 'positioned' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being located somewhere is a plain synonym for being placed there.

clue.text: Skin from dead mare flayed

parts.note: d is a standard abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies

indicators.note: flayed means torn apart, so the letters of the horse are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Hide taken off a lifeless female horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flayed' fits the skinning picture, but here it tears the horse's letters apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The true skin beneath the epidermis, the dermis, has this alternative medical name.

clue.text: Dog caught Hardy

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Oliver Hardy, of Laurel and Hardy, was known as Ollie

explanation.surface: A canine was captured, says a tough man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' is not tough but the comedian Oliver Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepdog breed from Scotland, of which the Border variety is the best known.

clue.text: Projection — one that's often found aboard

definitions.meaning: an arm on a windmill or a submarine's tower sticking out from the body
a canvas sheet rigged on a boat to catch the wind

explanation.surface: A protruding part, the kind usually on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A windmill's vanes stick out and are called by this name; a yacht carries canvas of the same name.

clue.text: Flowing drink left out smells awful

parts.note: the drink is a slang term for the sea

indicators.note: awful suggests something messed up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
out means removed from the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fluent prose, the drink abandoned, stinks terribly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' is slang for the sea, and 'left out' splits into the letter L and the removal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Smooth, uninterrupted motion or prose with no joins or breaks is described this way.

clue.text: Ether may make you number

indicators.note: may make you suggests the letters can be rebuilt into something new

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An anaesthetic can render you less sensitive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like 'more numb', which suits ether; it is the figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A small figure, the count between two and four, is a cardinal number.

clue.text: Salt or seaman — treat slightly differently

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: slightly differently tells us to rearrange the letters of treat

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An old sailor or sailor-type is handled in a different way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like a sailor beside 'seaman', but it is the chemical; TREAT rearranged gives TRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A compound of tartaric acid, such as cream of tartar, is a chemical salt.

clue.text: Rest of letters read out

indicators.note: read out means spoken, so we want a word sounding like the letters named

parts.note: two of the fifth letter of the alphabet, Es

explanation.surface: The remainder of the correspondence is read to an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest of letters' looks like the remainder of the post; the letters are Es, spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxation or repose; to take one's leisure is a synonym for resting.

clue.text: Get clean? It is sensible to go without

indicators.note: to go without here means to sit outside the other piece

parts.note: a sane person is sensible and rational
taken as written

explanation.surface: Should one quit drugs? Prudence says do without.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go without' reads as abstain, but 'without' is the old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinfect or make hygienic is to rid something of germs.

clue.text: Sour beer and a fizzing lager

indicators.note: fizzing suggests letters bubbling about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Stale ale alongside a bubbly pils.
explanation.definitionFit: Malt vinegar made from soured ale is the old sense of this word, literally sharp ale.

clue.text: Girl's lousy dinner in outskirts of Aberdare

definitions.note: the possessive 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece
outskirts of means only the first and last letters of the town name
lousy means bad, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman's poor supper on the edge of a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: Aberdare is a town in South Wales; only its first and last letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A female forename, the French form related to Adrian, is a girl's name.

clue.text: Compasses are no good in reserve

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated a

explanation.surface: Drawing instruments are useless when held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compasses' is the verb, not the drawing instrument; 'are' is the metric unit of area.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranges and compasses both mean the extent or scope of something, as in a singer's range.

clue.text: Receiver's cutting edge?

parts.note: the blade a recipient of post uses to slit envelopes

explanation.surface: Sounds like the latest technology in a radio set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receiver' suggests a radio or telephone; it is the person receiving mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A paperknife used to slit envelopes open is the blade a mail recipient uses.

clue.text: Follow the story as it's read

indicators.note: as it's read means spoken aloud, so a soundalike word is wanted

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Keep up with the narrative while it is recited.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow someone secretly, as a detective does, is to trail or follow them.

clue.text: Knock up a short piece of prose

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a rap is a knock on a door

explanation.surface: Dash off a brief passage of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock up' looks like a phrase for making something quickly; 'up' only turns RAP over.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragraph is a piece of prose, and the abbreviated form is a shortened word for it.

clue.text: Leave out ring Timothy returned

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

indicators.note: returned means read backwards

parts.note: Tim is the short form of Timothy; the letters also happen to appear reversed inside the full name, a coincidence the setter did not intend

explanation.surface: Skip the call to a man named Timothy that was given back.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude or skip something is a direct synonym for leaving it out.

clue.text: Weapon, one with German mark indicating damage on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside means the mark goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a scar is a mark left by injury
I is the Roman numeral one
mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: An arm bearing a German currency sign showing harm on its surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German mark' wants M; instead 'with German' gives MIT and 'mark indicating damage' gives SCAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved sword of Middle Eastern origin is a classic edged weapon.

clue.text: Help when family member needed

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a sister is a member of one's family

explanation.surface: Aid arrives once a relative is called upon.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who aids, a helper, can be called the help, as in hired help.
